newsitem.title: IRAN: New Iran president sends signals of moderation.
newsitem.headline: New Iran president sends signals of moderation.

text.p: Iran's new president, Mohammad Khatami, was formally sworn in on Monday and said the Islamic republic was eager to defuse world tension.
"My government considers dialogue between civilisations in the present world essential and will avoid any action or behaviour causing tension," he told parliament after taking the oath of office.
"We will have relations with any government that observes our independence, meaning the decisions made within our national interests," he added.
"But we will resist any power wishing to exercise dominance over us," a reference taken by diplomats and analysts to mean Iran's arch-foe the United States.

Khatami, a 54-year-old middle-level Shi'ite Moslem clergyman with a reputation as a moderate politician, became Iran's fifth president since the 1979 revolution toppled the monarchy and led to the creation of an Islamic republic.
He said Tehran would continue to "defend the rights of the Moslems and the oppressed, especially the Palestinian nation".
Iran, branded a rogue state by the United States for what Washington calls state sponsorship of "terrorism", wanted to play an active international role, the new president said.
But he vowed to "stand against the expansionism of the arrogant powers" -- the term Iran uses when referring to its declared enemies the United States and Israel.
Khatami was invited to take the oath of office by parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri -- the conservative he defeated by an overwhelming majority in May's presidential election.

Khatami, elected by a broad coalition of voters hoping for economic and social reforms, made several references to the need for national unity, social justice, respect for civil rights, the rule of law and eradicating the poverty of Iranians.

"Although it was carefully worded, the message was very strong," an Arab ambassador said after the speech. "He says we (clergymen) must have a dialogue with the people who are the reference point and respect personal freedoms."

Khatami, head of the country's executive power, listed the main goals of his four-year term as "protecting freedom and respect for the rights of people, expansion and deepening of a civil society, preventing violation of legal rights and liberties and provide freedom of expression and comfort of mind for every individual..."

Soon after the ceremony Khatami named his first appointment, keeping first vice-president Hassan Habibi in the post he held in the administration of outgoing president Akhbar Hashemi Rafsanjani. Habibi also acts as government spokesman.
Khatami said "a large pool of competent personalities" offered many choices for his cabinet, which he must present to parliament for approval within two weeks.
Quoted by the official news agency IRNA, Khatami said the search for ministers began immediately after the May 23 election.
Khatami's choice of cabinet ministers is likely to provide the first test of strength with the 270 members of the conservative-dominated parliament.
